chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
Regarding the man who urinates and forgets to wash his manhood until he performs ablution and prays, he said: He should wash his manhood and repeat the prayer, and he does not repeat the ablution.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets to clean oneself after urination before praying?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between major impurity (hadath) and minor impurity (najis al-badan), establishing that forgetting istinja does not invalidate the wudu already performed. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the prayer is invalidated by the presence of impurity on the body but the ablution remains valid, requiring only the cleansing of the specific area and a repetition of the prayer.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of our companions,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the man who urinates and forgets to wash his manhood until he performs Ablution (Wudhu), and he prays Salaat. Heasws said: ‘He should wash his manhood and he should repeat the Salaat, and he would not repeat the Ablution (Wudhu)’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Zur’ah, from Sama‘ah who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘After using toilet if you forget to wash clean your buttocks (because of feces) and take Wudu’, then remember after performing Salah (prayer), you must perform your Salah (prayer) again. If you wash your buttocks clean but forget washing your urethra clean and perform Salah (prayer), you must take Wudu’, wash your urethra and perform your Salah (prayer) again. It is because urine is not like feces.’”
